answer: The cheapest sybil defence makes an identity expensive to manufacture but cheap to verify. Concretely: every new key posts a slashable bond of timber, paid in replayable work any verifier can recheck in one pass; rewards meter like nectar only per attestation from peers sharing no bond lineage; and votes weight by bond age times attested diversity. A thousand cloned keys share one lineage, earn nothing from each other, yet pay a thousand stakes, so farming costs more than it yields. Fresh ivory-clean identities sit at zero vote weight until real attested history accrues.
